history.heading: Cradle of humankind
paragraphs: Ethiopia is one of the oldest places of human habitation. Fossils such as "Lucy" (Australopithecus afarensis, about 3.2 million years old) and some of the earliest known Homo sapiens were found there.

The Kingdom of Aksum, which flourished from around the 1st century CE, was a major trading power that minted its own coins and erected giant stone obelisks (stelae). Aksum adopted Christianity in the 4th century, making it one of the first Christian states.

history.heading: Medieval and Solomonic Ethiopia
paragraphs: The Zagwe dynasty built the remarkable rock-hewn churches of Lalibela in the 12th and 13th centuries. In 1270 the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba, came to power and ruled, with interruptions, until 1974.

Gondar became the capital in the 17th century, with castles that are now a UNESCO site. A period of fragmentation known as the Era of the Princes lasted until Emperor Tewodros II reunited the country in the 1850s.

history.heading: Resisting colonialism
paragraphs: Emperor Menelik II expanded the empire southward and defeated an Italian invasion at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, making Ethiopia one of only two African countries never colonised. Adwa became a symbol of African independence.
Fascist Italy invaded in 1935 and occupied the country until 1941. Emperor Haile Selassie returned and ruled until 1974; he was revered by the Rastafari movement in Jamaica.

history.heading: Revolution and federal Ethiopia
paragraphs: Amid famine, a Marxist military junta, the Derg, overthrew Haile Selassie in 1974. Under Mengistu Haile Mariam, its "Red Terror" killed tens of thousands, and the 1983–85 famine killed hundreds of thousands. Rebels led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front overthrew the Derg in 1991, and Eritrea became independent in 1993.

Abiy Ahmed became prime minister in 2018 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019 for making peace with Eritrea. A devastating war in Tigray from 2020 to 2022 killed hundreds of thousands of people. Conflicts in the Amhara and Oromia regions continue.

culture.heading: Ancient traditions
paragraphs: Ethiopia has its own script, Ge'ez (fidel), its own calendar, about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar, and its own system of telling time. Amharic is the federal working language, and Oromo, Tigrinya, Somali and Afar are among more than 80 languages spoken.

The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church is one of the oldest Christian churches, and Islam has a long history; Harar is considered a holy city of Islam. Timkat (Epiphany) and Meskel are spectacular religious festivals.

culture.heading: Coffee and cuisine
paragraphs: Ethiopia is the birthplace of coffee, and the traditional coffee ceremony is an important ritual of hospitality. Injera, a sourdough flatbread made from teff, is served with spicy stews (wat) and many vegan dishes eaten during frequent fasting periods.
Ethiopian runners, such as Abebe Bikila, Haile Gebrselassie and Tirunesh Dibaba, are among the greatest long-distance athletes in history.

politics.heading: Ethnic federalism
paragraphs: Ethiopia is a federal parliamentary republic organised largely along ethnic lines, with regional states that have considerable autonomy. The prime minister leads the government; the ruling Prosperity Party, created by Abiy Ahmed in 2019, dominates parliament.
Ethnic tensions, armed conflict, restrictions on media and human rights abuses are major concerns.

politics.heading: Regional role
paragraphs: Ethiopia is Africa's second most populous country, and Addis Ababa hosts the African Union headquarters. Its Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, inaugurated in 2025, has caused tensions with Egypt and Sudan. Ethiopia, which is landlocked, seeks access to the sea, a source of tension with Eritrea and Somalia.

economy.heading: Rapid growth
paragraphs: Ethiopia was one of the world's fastest-growing economies in the 2000s and 2010s, driven by state-led investment in infrastructure, industrial parks and hydropower. Agriculture still employs most of the population, and coffee is the leading export, along with flowers, oilseeds and gold.
Ethiopian Airlines is Africa's largest and most successful airline.

economy.heading: Challenges
paragraphs: Conflict, inflation, foreign currency shortages and debt have strained the economy. In 2024 the government floated the birr, its currency, as part of reforms backed by the IMF, and it restructured its debt. Drought and food insecurity affect millions of people.
